test_page.gdpr_consent_body: I agree to the processing of my responses for psychological and perceptual assessment.
test_page.stage1_desc: Measuring general cognitive ability and problem-solving skills.
test_page.stage1_instr: 11 short reasoning questions — numbers, words, shapes. Answer each one; you have 45 seconds per question. The timer is shown at the top of the screen. Expected time: ~10 minutes.
test_page.stage2_desc: Assessing workplace emotional intelligence and self-awareness.
test_page.stage2_instr: 16 statements — choose how much you agree on a 1–5 scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). You have 45 seconds per statement. Expected time: ~8 minutes.
test_page.stage3_desc: Evaluating social perceptiveness and non-verbal emotion appraisal.
test_page.stage3_instr: In this short task you'll see a series of facial expressions. For each one, decide whether it looks spontaneous or posed. Trust your first impression — there are no trick questions. Expected time: ~2 minutes.
test_page.instr_ack: I have read and understand these instructions.

nav.guide.tooltip: How to run assessments and interpret results
guide.title: Recruiter Guide
guide.s1.title: What preSift is
guide.s1.body: preSift gives you two views of the same person, side by side: what the candidate says about themselves and how they perform on real tasks. It does not replace the interview — it supports it with measurable data, so you enter the conversation with evidence instead of guesses.
guide.s2.title: The three modules
guide.s2.m1: Logic & Reasoning — 11 short tasks (numerical, verbal, abstract). 45-second limit per question.
guide.s2.m3: Emotion Perception — short videos; the candidate decides whether the smile is spontaneous or posed.
guide.s2.note: The first two measure ability; the third measures perception, not truthfulness. All three are indicative, not diagnostic.
guide.s3.title: How it works, step by step
guide.s3.b1: You create an assessment link for a specific role (uses 1 credit).
guide.s3.b2: You send the link to the candidate — no account needed.
guide.s3.b3: The candidate consents (GDPR), reads the instructions and begins.
guide.s3.b4: On completion, the report appears in your dashboard.
guide.s3.b5: You export results to PDF/CSV and fold them into your process.
guide.s4.title: Rules of use
guide.s4.r1: The human decides. preSift is never the sole criterion for hiring or rejection.
guide.s4.r2: Results show a tendency, not certainty. A low score does not mean "unsuitable".
guide.s4.r3: The candidate never sees scores. They see only a thank-you page; the interpretation is for you.
guide.s4.r4: Always interpret alongside CV, interview and references.
guide.s5.title: Legal duties
guide.s5.l1: As the employer/client, you are the controller of the candidate data.
guide.s5.l2: Use the data only for the current assessment process.
guide.s5.l3: The candidate can download or delete their data at any time from the completion page.
guide.s5.l4: Roles and obligations in full: the Data Processing Agreement (/dpa) and the Privacy Notice (/privacy).
guide.s6.title: Practicalities
guide.s6.p1: Credits: 1 credit per assessment link, charged when the link is created.
guide.s6.p2: Integrity: copy and the right-click menu are blocked; focus/window deviations are recorded and may flag the attempt.
guide.s6.p3: Export: PDF for one candidate, CSV for bulk analysis.
guide.s6.p4: Archiving: candidates are archived, not deleted, so your history is preserved.
guide.s7.title: Frequently asked questions
guide.s7.q1: Does the candidate see their score? No — only you do.
guide.s7.q2: How long does it take? About 15–20 minutes in total.
guide.s7.q3: Can they retake it? A new link means a new credit. There is no "reset".
guide.s7.q4: What does "Strong/Moderate/Low fit" mean? It is an overall indicator based on percentile — not a verdict.
guide.s7.q5: What is the "Integrity Flag"? An indication that something in the attempt was not clean; check it before judging.
